raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
# What does this PR do?

`list_checkpoints()` (used to populate the checkpoint-path dropdown in
the WebUI) only listed the *immediate* children of the model/finetuning
save dir and checked each one directly for adapter weight files. That
matches a run that finished normally, since its final adapter is saved
directly under the run directory (`<run_dir>/adapter_model.safetensors`).
It does **not** match an intermediate `save_steps` checkpoint, which is
saved one level deeper as `<run_dir>/checkpoint-<step>/adapter_model.safetensors`
— e.g. exactly what's left behind when a run is interrupted (ctrl-c)
before it reaches its final save. Those nested checkpoints were silently
skipped, so with multiple runs in the output directory the dropdown
appeared to only show part of what was actually on disk (#9766).

This PR:
- Changes `list_checkpoints()` to scan the two levels under `save_dir`
  that can hold a checkpoint — `<run_dir>` and `<run_dir>/checkpoint-<step>`
  — instead of a single `os.listdir()`, so both top-level (finished-run)
  and nested (intermediate) checkpoints are discovered. The scan is
  deliberately bounded rather than an `os.walk`: save dirs also hold
  `runs/`, `wandb/` and exported models, and `list_checkpoints` fires on
  every model / finetuning-type change in the UI.
- Sorts the dropdown run by run: runs by name (timestamped names are
  chronological), then each run's own entry, then its `checkpoint-<step>`
  entries by numeric step, so `checkpoint-200` precedes `checkpoint-1000`.
- Adds `get_checkpoint_dir()`, which maps a checkpoint-dropdown value to its
  real directory when it names an existing checkpoint under the save dir, so
  nested checkpoint values resolve correctly. `get_save_dir()` keeps main's
  rule: a value that contains the platform path separator is returned
  unchanged, so a user-typed relative `output_dir` with the native separator still
  resolves against the cwd.

## How was this tested?

Added `tests/webui/test_control_checkpoints.py`:
- `list_checkpoints()` finds both a top-level (finished-run) checkpoint
  and nested intermediate checkpoints in a fixture directory tree that
  mirrors the report (a completed run + an interrupted run with only
  `checkpoint-100`/`checkpoint-200` subfolders).
- `list_checkpoints()` still returns an empty list when there's nothing
  to find.
- `get_checkpoint_dir()` resolves a nested checkpoint value to its directory
  under the save dir.
- `get_save_dir()` still bypasses the save dir entirely for an absolute
  custom path (regression guard for #4292).
- `checkpoint-100`/`checkpoint-200`/`checkpoint-1000` come back in step
  order, not lexicographic order.
- A checkpoint sitting in `save_dir` itself does not surface as a `"."`
  dropdown entry.
- `runs/` and `wandb/` under the save dir are not listed.
- A finished run keeps its intermediate checkpoints selectable alongside
  its final save.
- Runs and their checkpoints stay grouped when they are mixed: an older run's
  `checkpoint-100` sorts under that run, not after a newer run.

```
$ WANDB_DISABLED=true python -m pytest -vv --import-mode=importlib tests/webui/test_control_checkpoints.py
15 passed
```

I also reproduced the bug against `main` first with a small script
building the same fixture tree, confirming only the finished-run
checkpoint was listed and the two nested ones were missing.

Fixes #9766

## Before submitting

- [x] Did you read the [contributor guideline](https://github.com/hiyouga/LLaMA-Factory/blob/main/.github/CONTRIBUTING.md)?
- [x] Did you write any new necessary tests?

The comment says "nested one level deeper", but `os.walk` descends without limit and nothing prunes after a hit, so this also walks into every `checkpoint-*/` it just matched, plus `runs/`, `wandb/` and any exported model dir under the save dir. `list_checkpoints` fires on every model and finetuning-type change in the UI, so on a save dir with a few finished runs this turns into a full tree stat each time.

Adding `dirs[:] = []` once a checkpoint is found, and capping the depth at one level, would match both the comment and the issue being fixed.

nodes.body:
Right on both counts — the comment described a bounded scan and the code did not do one. Fixed in d0b0a2c1 by dropping `os.walk` for an explicit scan of exactly the two levels that can hold a checkpoint: `<run_dir>` and `<run_dir>/checkpoint-<step>`. Cost is now one `listdir` of the save dir plus one per run dir, so `runs/`, `wandb/` and exported model dirs get a single `listdir` each rather than a full descent.

One deliberate difference from your suggestion: I did not stop at the first hit inside a run dir. With the two-level scan there is no `checkpoint-*/` recursion left to avoid — those are the leaves — and continuing means a finished run keeps its intermediate `save_steps` checkpoints selectable alongside its final save, which is the case #9766 is about. `test_list_checkpoints_lists_intermediate_saves_of_a_finished_run` covers it. Happy to prune instead if you would rather the final save be the only entry for a completed run.

nodes.body:
You are right that this is user-visible and I had not called it out. Added a "Behavior change worth calling out" section to the PR description, and `get_save_dir`'s docstring now states it directly: only an absolute last component bypasses the save dir, a relative one is always joined under `saves/<model>/<finetuning_type>/`, and an absolute path is how to opt out.

I kept the `os.path.isabs()` semantics rather than trying to preserve the old relative-with-separator bypass, because the two cases are indistinguishable at the call site — `get_save_dir(model, finetuning_type, x)` is the same shape whether `x` came from the checkpoint dropdown or the free-text `output_dir` box. Honouring an embedded separator would send the nested dropdown values outside the save dir, which is the bug this PR fixes. If you would rather not take the `output_dir` regression at all, the alternative is threading a flag through the two `runner.py` call sites so only the checkpoint path gets the strict treatment — say the word and I will do that instead.

nodes.body:
Correction to my earlier reply in this thread: I no longer keep the `os.path.isabs()` semantics. d9987e4a restores `get_save_dir()` to main's rule, so a value containing the platform path separator is returned unchanged. A user-typed relative `output_dir` such as `my\custom\dir` on Windows (`my/custom/dir` on POSIX) resolves against the cwd again. On Windows, a forward-slash path such as `my/custom/dir` is still joined under the save dir, as it is on main.

Nested values from the checkpoint dropdown go through `get_checkpoint_dir()`, which resolves a value under the save dir when it names an existing checkpoint there. `test_get_save_dir_keeps_relative_custom_path_against_cwd` covers the native-separator case.

The "Behavior change worth calling out" section of the PR description described the `isabs()` behavior, so I am removing it.

inline_comments.body:
The comment says "nested one level deeper", but `os.walk` descends without limit and nothing prunes after a hit, so this also walks into every `checkpoint-*/` it just matched, plus `runs/`, `wandb/` and any exported model dir under the save dir. `list_checkpoints` fires on every model and finetuning-type change in the UI, so on a save dir with a few finished runs this turns into a full tree stat each time.

Adding `dirs[:] = []` once a checkpoint is found, and capping the depth at one level, would match both the comment and the issue being fixed.

Right on both counts — the comment described a bounded scan and the code did not do one. Fixed in d0b0a2c1 by dropping `os.walk` for an explicit scan of exactly the two levels that can hold a checkpoint: `<run_dir>` and `<run_dir>/checkpoint-<step>`. Cost is now one `listdir` of the save dir plus one per run dir, so `runs/`, `wandb/` and exported model dirs get a single `listdir` each rather than a full descent.

One deliberate difference from your suggestion: I did not stop at the first hit inside a run dir. With the two-level scan there is no `checkpoint-*/` recursion left to avoid — those are the leaves — and continuing means a finished run keeps its intermediate `save_steps` checkpoints selectable alongside its final save, which is the case #9766 is about. `test_list_checkpoints_lists_intermediate_saves_of_a_finished_run` covers it. Happy to prune instead if you would rather the final save be the only entry for a completed run.

You are right that this is user-visible and I had not called it out. Added a "Behavior change worth calling out" section to the PR description, and `get_save_dir`'s docstring now states it directly: only an absolute last component bypasses the save dir, a relative one is always joined under `saves/<model>/<finetuning_type>/`, and an absolute path is how to opt out.

I kept the `os.path.isabs()` semantics rather than trying to preserve the old relative-with-separator bypass, because the two cases are indistinguishable at the call site — `get_save_dir(model, finetuning_type, x)` is the same shape whether `x` came from the checkpoint dropdown or the free-text `output_dir` box. Honouring an embedded separator would send the nested dropdown values outside the save dir, which is the bug this PR fixes. If you would rather not take the `output_dir` regression at all, the alternative is threading a flag through the two `runner.py` call sites so only the checkpoint path gets the strict treatment — say the word and I will do that instead.

inline_comments.body:
Correction to my earlier reply in this thread: I no longer keep the `os.path.isabs()` semantics. d9987e4a restores `get_save_dir()` to main's rule, so a value containing the platform path separator is returned unchanged. A user-typed relative `output_dir` such as `my\custom\dir` on Windows (`my/custom/dir` on POSIX) resolves against the cwd again. On Windows, a forward-slash path such as `my/custom/dir` is still joined under the save dir, as it is on main.

Nested values from the checkpoint dropdown go through `get_checkpoint_dir()`, which resolves a value under the save dir when it names an existing checkpoint there. `test_get_save_dir_keeps_relative_custom_path_against_cwd` covers the native-separator case.

The "Behavior change worth calling out" section of the PR description described the `isabs()` behavior, so I am removing it.
